newsitem.title: YEMEN: Trial starts of Yemen schools shooting suspect.
newsitem.headline: Trial starts of Yemen schools shooting suspect.

text.p: A man accused of the shooting deaths of six children, a school headmistress and a teacher in an attack on hundreds of pupils at two schools went on trial on Monday in a courtroom packed with hundreds of enraged people.
Witnesses at the Sanaa courtroom said Mohammad Ahmad Misleh al-Nazari was brought into a steel cage from a side door on a wheelchair.
He was sporting a long, thick beard and wearing a long grey Arab robe. He was flanked by armed policemen.

The Yemeni man was wounded in an exchange of fire with police on Sunday after he opened fire from an assault rifle on hundreds of students aged between six and 18 as they lined up at two schools to go into morning classes.
The headmistress of Tala'eh school, a teacher in his 30s from Musa Ibn Naseer school and six pupils were killed.
An Interior Ministry statement said 11 pupils from the two neighbouring schools and three other people were wounded.
More than 2,000 people, including students from the two schools and their parents, gathered in the street outside the courthouse under heavy security.
Grim-faced and angry, many said they were shocked by the first such crime in Yemen and called for the death penalty.
"We expect and want a quick sentencing to this ugly crime," said 15-year-old Hamza Ali Ahmed, a student from Talae'h.
"We will not have peace of mind until the killer is executed," said Mansour Serhan, 16, from Musa Ibn Naseer school.
It was not immediately clear when the trial would finish, but it is being held at the court for emergency cases at the court of appeal, indicating the three-judge panel might reach a quick verdict.
Police had arrested the gunman after an exchange of fire with security forces in which he was wounded in the leg as he tried to escape. None of the security forces was reported hurt.
Witnesses described the assailant as a disgruntled former bus driver who had been sacked by the headmistress at the Tala'eh school.
A security official named the headmistress as Asma Noman, an Egyptian woman in her 40s whose son was also killed.

Prosecutor-General Mohammad al-Badri told the official news agency SABA on Sunday night that the prosecutor's office in the southern part of Sanaa had completed its interrogation of the suspect and "it was decided to try him on Monday at the court for emergency matters at the court of appeal".
A security official said he believed the assailant was insane. Yemeni television on Sunday night quoted investigation sources as saying the man was schizophrenic.
